notes.checkpoints: AUTHORED IN T5 (plan Task 7) AND CROSS-VERIFIED BEFORE ENROLLMENT. Ten checkpoints, 38 assertions. Every `equals` is derived from the RECORDING, never from a player's output: text and attribute values from the segment's initial_dom attrs, changed values from the dom.attr event that changed them, form values from the input.value event that typed them, and every `exists: false` from a dom.remove naming that node or an ancestor of it. Each `t` sits strictly between the last event it must include and the first it must exclude, so no player has to adjudicate a float tie. CROSS-VERIFICATION: all ten were executed by the FORK's player first (jspsych-replay-fork, tests/checkpoints.test.ts, commit 7dd9ee5, over a byte-identical copy of this fixture — the fork checksum-pins those bytes on its side and CH re-verified the match) and only then enrolled here — CH's viewer must never be its own conformance definition. Evidence: .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-11-t5-a2-viewer-migration/task-7a-crosscheck.md. The pin is one-directional, exactly like the fork's fixture checksum: an edit HERE leaves the fork green until someone re-copies, so a deliberate revision has to land both sides together. COVERAGE: the two fullscreen transitions as DOM state (segments 1 and 13 — the format has no prop for the transition itself, they are lane events); the dom.attr-driven class change plus the five disabled writes (segment 6); the sketchpad canvas as a NODE and dom.attr in both directions, set to "" and removed by `value: null` (segment 9); survey form state mid-typing and complete, plus both teardowns including nodes that go with a removed ANCESTOR rather than being named by the dom.remove (node 20 under node 19 in segment 9; nodes 9 and 17 under the form, node 5, in segment 12). WHAT `exists: false` MEASURES, precisely: both players read it as `resolves && isConnected`, so it says the node is off the page, not that the id map was purged of it. Measured with a fault injection — a viewer whose dom.remove purges the named node but not its descendants leaves every checkpoint here green, because the descendants are detached either way. The map purge itself is pinned CH-side in tests/replay/dom-patch.test.js (T5.3). NOT AUTHORED: any canvas PIXEL assertion — the four props read text, existence, form value and attributes, and a shared pixel prop would need per-player semantics neither repo has agreed (the fork's player paints with allow-scripts, CH's script-less frame cannot be pixel-read through the id map at all); segment 9's final canvas.snapshot at t=5097.3, which targets the node its own dom.remove has just taken out (indices 80/81, the dangling-reference specimen); segment 8's canvas box, which the sandbox lays out at 436x327 for a 400x300 bitmap; and anything reading an alignment status, since this fixture carries zero camera and zero anchor blocks across all 909 events.
notes.no_redaction_leak: Holds VACUOUSLY. jsPsych v1 has no redaction, so no event in this fixture carries a `redacted` marker and the typed survey answers sit in plaintext input.value. The invariant is listed because it is ALWAYS_ON in the runner, not because this fixture exercises it — canonical-core is what proves the privacy floor bites.
notes.media_gap: KNOWN LIMITATION. This fixture carries zero media.* events: the vendored replay-test-suite timeline has no audio or video trial (the bench loads plugin-html-audio-response only for its own grafted trials, which the suite does not include). The media spot check the converter design sketches is therefore NOT satisfiable from this timeline, and media coverage needs a different timeline rather than a different driver. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT, for whoever picks it up in T7 or later: add an audio trial to bench/harness/trials/replay-test-suite.js using plugin-html-audio-response (the bench already loads it, so the pin covers it) plus a video plugin alongside, then re-cut through the same harness; or, if a real timeline is not wanted, hand-author a synthetic media fixture as a separate corpus entry. Either way it is a new fixture, not an amendment to this one.
notes.canvas_split: The 2-full-baseline / 9-region-diff split is asserted in two places, neither of them here in full: all 9 region rectangles are spot-checked above by value, and tests/tools/convert.test.js asserts the exact 2/9 split, because the expectations format has no way to say a key is ABSENT and 'full baseline' means 'no region key'. The fork's smoke test asserts the same split on its copy.
notes.other_absent_event_types: clipboard.*, touch.*, input.select, scroll.element, focus/blur, visibility.*, dom.text, recording.capture_stopped — all consequences of the timeline (no <select>, no touch device, no clipboard trial, the window never loses focus), not of the converter.
notes.stylesheets: stylesheets[0] is the pinned jsPsych stylesheet with its real CSS text (470,464 chars, most of it @fontsource Open Sans embedded as base64 woff2), because the recording harness serves the pinned CSS from its own origin — a cross-origin sheet has unreadable cssRules and the v1 recorder can then only write css: null. Its href accordingly carries the 127.0.0.1 origin and ephemeral port of the recording run, which is where the page genuinely loaded it from; the href is deliberately not spot-checked, since the port changes on every regeneration. The 703-char inline sheet added and removed by the sketchpad plugin is what makes stylesheet_events non-empty. RE-CUT COST: 460KB of those chars are 32 base64 woff2 blobs, so re-cutting this fixture writes ~1.7MB of compressed, permanent git history across three repos (raw capture + this fixture + the fork's copy). Re-cuts should be deliberate; the guardian test already forces that.
